Placement data enters NIRF through Graduation Outcomes, one of five parameters, which carries 20 percent of the total score. Placement-linked sub-parameters make up the majority of that 20, so placement contributes roughly a low double-digit share of an institution’s overall NIRF score.

The first place a rank drop shows up is not the newspaper. It is the admissions office phone in June, where the questions get shorter and the negotiations about fees get longer.

Leadership teams tend to treat rankings as reputation, something the marketing head should handle. That framing costs money. One academic year is realistic if work starts before the season opens.
